summary: Exact bounded geometric input domain from qualified G331; full supports and conductor fibres retained, n-1 arity, degree-n component convention, no product grant.
detailedSummary: Fixes proper primary reference data, defines bounded inputs in the actual decreasing completion, admits zero and mixed-zero inputs belonging to that class, and excludes all bottom/unbounded inputs. Uses only the supplied independent cone/comparison, compact topology, density, and full descent. Dimension zero is empty and curves have zero potential entries.
text:
# n1. Domain, reference data, and the retained grant

This manuscript is a partial result for P12.4, not a solution claim. The only supplied result used is qualified G331, including its entire source, mandatory annotation, source ledger, and exact scope. ROOT338 is an unreviewed approach, not a premise. No envelope, intersection, product, energy, locality, or arbitrary-model cofinality theorem is imported from G331.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be excellent, reduced, local, and of positive dimension $n$. Put $X_{\mathfrak a}=\{v:v(\mathfrak a)=1\}$ for a fixed proper $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal $\mathfrak a$. A point is a centred real semivaluation on $R$ with $0<v(\mathfrak m)<\infty$; its prime support may be nonminimal. Every such support is retained, including supports on the conductor quotient. Ideal values mean minima on a finite generating set. In particular primary ideal values are finite, positive, continuous, and bounded on $X_{\mathfrak a}$. Units have value zero. G331 gives the compact Hausdorff boundary and the exact primary change $T(v)=v/v(\mathfrak b)$.

The geometric core was defined before ideal closure: actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. G331 proves that its uniform closure $C=C_{\rm geom}$ equals the uniform closure of finite nonnegative real combinations of $-v(I)$, where $I$ is primary or the unit ideal. Its completion $D=D_{\rm geom}$ consists of infima of ACTUAL nonempty decreasing $C$-nets, with the identically $-\infty$ function allowed. We use only this completion, not closure under arbitrary infima, increasing limits, or flattened nested nets.

The product-input domain in this manuscript is
$$D^{\rm bd}_{\mathfrak a}=\{u\in D:-M\le u\le0\text{ for some finite }M\}.$$
This includes every bounded real, discontinuous completed input, zero, and permitted mixed-zero branch patterns. It excludes every input having a $-\infty$ value, including bottom. Every continuous input in $C$ is bounded. Existence of a bounded decreasing representation needs no truncation: if $g_\alpha\downarrow u$ and $u\ge-M$, then $g_\alpha\ge u\ge-M$ and $g_\alpha\le0$.

Use $p=n-1$ potential entries; a test supplies the nth intersection entry. For non-equidimensional $R$, all algebraic moments below use the degree-$n$ part of the primary length polynomial. Lower-dimensional components remain in the boundary and domain, but contribute zero in this chosen convention. A separate lower-dimensional product would have a different arity; none is silently added. In dimension one there are zero potentials and a reference measure, constructed geometrically in n5. For dimension zero the reduced local ring is a field, the centred boundary is empty, and the measure is the unique zero measure; there is no negative-arity assertion.

G331 also supplies two specific functional facts used below. Rational profiles $-v(I)/k$ with $k\in\mathbb N_{>0}$ (unit allowed) are uniformly dense in $C$. The rational difference span of ideal gauges is a lattice, contains rational constants since $v(\mathfrak a)=1$, and is uniformly dense in $C(X_{\mathfrak a},\mathbb R)$. To recall the mechanism, a common denominator turns any span element into $(v(J)-v(K))/k$, and
$$\min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH).$$
The bounded truncations $v((f)+\mathfrak a^N)=\min(v(f),N)$ separate all semivaluations, including infinite coordinates. Uniform closure of this rational lattice is a real vector lattice; the compact lattice approximation argument yields all real continuous tests. This is density on the entire compact boundary, not a finite grid.

For a finite normalization $R\hookrightarrow S$, G331 retains the disjoint local normal centres above $\mathfrak m$ and their FULL restriction fibres. At finite conductor value the fibre is a singleton. At infinite conductor value the identification is exactly equality on the conductor quotient. Continuous and completed geometric functions descend precisely when constant on these whole fibres. We do not select one lift or discard an infinity stratum. Normalization in n4 is applied only to actual pullbacks of downstairs functions.

For nonreduced germs the present data are those of the reduction and the reduced gauge. No nilpotent generic length is reconstructed; n6 proves an explicit obstruction to doing so from these data alone. P12.5 energy and general finite-map geometric operators in P12.6 are outside the results here.

The paper and local notes give mathematical draft arguments; hashing, compilation, and finite diagnostics are separate evidence. The entire G331 source/annotation/ledger are retained under inputs/mathematical. Rerun data retention: `python audit_inputs.py`. New source applications are recorded in source-application-ledger.md.
